scope: Complete sequential reading of both local problem-collection PDFs. Coverage summaries describe the questions/comments and bibliography actually read; they are not proofs of referenced results.

section_coverage.summary: Title, eight authors, 2014-12-08 date, abstract and contents; the abstract frames the document as a Boolean-function open-problem collection.
Explains the 2012 list and the 2013 Simons special-semester collection; points to O’Donnell’s book for background.

Defines the uniform cube, inner product, Fourier coefficients, Parseval/variance, degree, influence and noise operator; physical p. 2 literally prints a product in the character exponent, inconsistent for |S|>1 with the asserted orthonormal Fourier basis. The standard/intended Walsh character uses a sum; singleton formulas agree either way.
Defines character expansion and the document’s noise operator convention on product alphabets.
States the Gaussian Ornstein–Uhlenbeck/noise operator used for real-domain questions.
Defines circuits, AC0/TC0 and deterministic/randomized decision trees; no theorem proof is developed here.

Lists cube Fourier, influence, threshold, testing and Gaussian polynomial questions with source attributions and historical remarks; A165 appears as “L0 sparsity of spectrum” on physical/printed p. 10 and B167 as “Low-degree polynomials and distance from indicators” on physical/printed p. 11.

section_coverage.unit: §4 Fourier analysis on the symmetric group
section_coverage.summary: States a FKN-type stability question for Sn and an edge-isoperimetry question in the transposition graph, with cited special cases.
Lists total-influence and noise-smoothing questions for bounded-degree real-valued cube functions.
Lists intersecting-family, graph, finite-field removal/sumset, PFR and hypercube routing questions with status remarks.
Covers Gaussian partitions/noise stability, correlation, sensitivity, PTF influence and spectral concentration conjectures and cited progress.
Lists two approximation-hardness questions: MAX-2-LIN on the hypercube and the republic predicate.
Read the full bibliography [AA11a]–[Yan07]; references identify candidate primary works but were not independently read in this batch.

Identifies Ben Green’s collection and its history (circulated since 2018; earlier manuscript from 2013); explains original numbering is retained when solved and records “Update 2025”, most recent update December 2025.
Problems 1–8 cover sum/product-free sets, Ulam sequences, arithmetic removal and updates, including items explicitly marked solved.
Problems 9–24 cover progression-free sets, random differences, corners, partition regularity and collinear configurations, with dated status remarks.
Problems 25–30 cover restricted sumsets, additive bases, approximate groups and density/doubling questions; Problem 28 is the independent integer-summand uniformity question.
Defines the additive B2/Sidon convention and discusses extremal Sidon bounds, gaps, autoconvolutions, matrix-multiplication questions and related examples.
Problems 37–42 cover arithmetic Kakeya, Shannon capacity, random translates, covering codes, the pyjama problem and sphere-packing linear programming.
Problems 43–48 discuss large/small sieves, Jacobsthal gaps, inverse large sieve and extremal sieve structure.
Problems 49–57 cover PFR/Bogolyubov, sumsets, additive complements, Gowers inverse theorems and structured functions, including 2023–2025 updates.
Problems 58–67 concern sumsets below square-root density, prime/square differences, Waring-type problems and updates.
Problems 68–77 discuss arcs, collinear configurations, grids, surfaces, no-three-in-line and Heilbronn-type questions.
Problems 78–80 concern small-set growth in groups, random generators/expansion and quantitative approximate-group classification.
Problems 81–84 discuss cosine/sine sums, inverse Littlewood, Fourier norms and flat Littlewood polynomials with updates.
Problems 85–100 span geometric incidence/covering, random structures, polynomial equations, solution counts and sofic/hyperlinear groups; updates include a November 2025 announcement.
Read the entire bibliography [1]–[313]; it supplies follow-up pointers, including [310] as the MathOverflow discussion cited by Problem 28, but no cited work was independently read here.
